title: 4. Autonomic Dysreflexia (AD)
source_document: English Master Data Collection & Clinical Content Repository

items: Definition: A life-threatening medical emergency characterized by an unmodulated, massive sympathetic response to noxious stimuli below the level of injury.
Threshold: Occurs almost exclusively in individuals with an SCI level at T6 or above.
Triggers: Distended bladder (most common; blocked catheter), bowel impaction, pressure injuries, tight clothing, ingrown toenails, acute surgical/medical abdomen.

Signs & Symptoms: Rapid, severe hypertension (systolic BP > 20–40 mmHg above baseline), pounding headache, profuse sweating and cutaneous flushing above the injury level, goosebumps (piloerection) and pale cold skin below the injury level, nasal congestion, bradycardia.

content.text: Autonomic Dysreflexia is a serious medical emergency. Seek immediate emergency medical assistance (call 112 in India or go to the nearest emergency room) right away for professional clinical assessment and intervention.

items: a. Recognize Warning Signs: Sudden severe pounding headache, sweating or skin flushing above the T6 injury level, goosebumps, cold clammy skin below the injury, or a rapid spike in blood pressure.

b. Immediate Medical Assistance Required: Autonomic Dysreflexia is a serious medical emergency. Seek immediate emergency medical assistance (call 112 in India or go to the nearest emergency room) right away for professional clinical assessment and intervention.
